topic.title: About my family
topic.description: Read a short paragraph about a family to learn how to write about family members, ages, and jobs.

readingPassage.title: My Family
readingPassage.text: My name is Sara and I'm 13 years old. I live in Madrid with my family. There are four people in my family: my father, my mother, my brother, and me. My father is named Carlos and he is a doctor. My mother is named Ana and she is a teacher. My brother, Pablo, is 10 years old and he loves playing football. We have a dog named Max.

tips: Use 'There are [number] people in my family' to start.
Use possessive adjectives like 'my father', 'my mother', and 'my brother'.
Use 'is' to state names, ages, and jobs (e.g., 'My father is a doctor').
Capitalize names, family titles used as names, cities, and languages.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: true or false
exercises.instruction: Read the text and decide if the statements are True or False.

questions.statement: Sara is 10 years old.
Sara's family lives in Madrid.
Sara's mother is a doctor.
Pablo is Sara's brother.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: gap fill
exercises.instruction: Fill in the missing words based on the reading passage.

questions.sentence: There are ________ people in Sara's family.
Sara's father works as a ________.
The family pet is a dog named ________.

discussion.question: How many people are there in your family? What are their names?

topic.title: A study diary
topic.description: Read a daily study log to practice writing about school tasks, study times, and subjects.

readingPassage.title: My Study Diary
readingPassage.text:
Monday:
- 4:00 PM: Read Chapter 3 of the History textbook.
- 5:30 PM: Do 10 English grammar exercises.

Tuesday:
- 4:30 PM: Practice maths problems on page 42.
- 6:00 PM: Learn 15 new Spanish vocabulary words.

Wednesday:
- 5:00 PM: Finish Science project poster.
- 7:00 PM: Rest and watch a movie.

tips: Use days of the week in chronological order.
Write time using 'AM' or 'PM' consistently.
Use action verbs to start tasks (e.g., 'Read', 'Do', 'Practice', 'Learn').
Keep entries concise using bullet points.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: multiple choice
exercises.instruction: Select the correct answer from the study diary.

questions.question: What subject does the student study at 4:30 PM on Tuesday?
When does the student finish the Science project poster?

exercises.title: Check your understanding: gap fill
exercises.instruction: Fill in the missing details from the study diary.

questions.sentence: On Monday at 5:30 PM, the student does 10 ________ grammar exercises.

discussion.question: Do you keep a study diary or a to-do list for your homework?

topic.title: A study date email
topic.description: Read an email between friends arranging a time and place to study together.

readingPassage.title: Email: Studying Together
readingPassage.text:
Subject: Study together for the English test?

Hi Ben,

Are you free to study together for our English test? We can meet at the city library on Thursday at 4:00 PM. We can review unit 4 and practice vocabulary.

Let me know if this time works for you!

Best,
Leo

tips: Include a clear, short subject line.
Use questions like 'Are you free to...?' to make suggestions.
Specify the day, time, and location clearly.
Close with a simple sign-off like 'Best' or 'See you soon'.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: true or false
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statements are True or False.

questions.statement: Leo wants to study for a maths test.
They plan to meet at the library.
The suggested meeting day is Thursday.

exercises.instruction: Fill in the missing words from the email.

topic.title: A school project poster
topic.description: Read a school poster about environmental protection to practice reading headings, bullet points, and simple rules.

readingPassage.title: Save Our Planet: Green School Project
readingPassage.text:
Help Us Keep Our School Green!

Easy steps for every student:
1. Recycle paper and plastic in the green bins.
2. Turn off the lights when leaving the classroom.
3. Turn off water taps completely after washing your hands.
4. Walk or ride a bicycle to school instead of coming by car.

Join the Green Club every Tuesday at lunchtime in Room 12!

tips: Use large, bold headers to grab attention.
Use imperative command verbs (e.g., 'Recycle', 'Turn off', 'Walk') for actions.
Keep rules short and easy to read.
Include call-to-action details at the bottom (time, place, club name).

topic.title: My favourite meal
topic.description: Read a description of a favorite meal to learn food vocabulary and expressions of taste.

readingPassage.title: My Favourite Meal
readingPassage.text: My favourite meal is dinner on Sunday. My dad makes homemade pizza. He puts tomato sauce, cheese, mushrooms, and chicken on top. I love eating it with a fresh salad and a glass of orange juice. For dessert, we have vanilla ice cream with strawberries. It is delicious!

tips: State which meal is your favourite (breakfast, lunch, or dinner).
List main ingredients using 'with', 'and', or 'on top'.
Use simple descriptive words like 'delicious', 'fresh', 'tasty', or 'sweet'.
Mention a drink and a dessert to complete the meal description.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: gap fill

topic.title: Meeting friends
topic.description: Read short text messages between friends making arrangements to meet up.

readingPassage.title: Text Messages: Weekend Plans
readingPassage.text:
Maya: Hi Tom! Are you free this Saturday afternoon?
Tom: Hi Maya! Yes, I am. What do you want to do?
Maya: Do you want to go to the park and play badminton?
Tom: That sounds fun! What time shall we meet?
Maya: Let's meet at 2:30 PM near the park entrance.
Tom: Great! See you on Saturday at 2:30.

tips: Start messages with informal greetings ('Hi', 'Hey').
Ask 'Do you want to...?' to invite someone to an activity.
Suggest a specific time and location.
Confirm agreement clearly ('Great!', 'See you then!').

topic.title: Introducing yourself on a blog
topic.description: Read a blog post introduction to learn how to present your name, country, hobbies, and interests online.

readingPassage.title: Blog Post: Welcome to My World!
readingPassage.text:
Hello world!

My name is Kenji and I am 14 years old. I am from Tokyo, Japan. I am a student at Sakura Middle School.

In my free time, I love playing video games, drawing manga, and listening to pop music. My favourite subject at school is Art because I love painting.

Welcome to my blog! Please leave a comment and tell me about yourself!

tips: Use 'Hello' or 'Welcome to my blog' to start.
State your name, age, country, and school.
List hobbies using 'In my free time, I love...' or 'My favourite...'.
Encourage readers to respond with 'Leave a comment'.

topic.title: Introducing yourself in an email
topic.description: Read an introductory email to an e-pal/penfriend to practice personal details and basic questions.

readingPassage.title: Email: Hello from France!
readingPassage.text:
Subject: Hello from your new e-pal!

Dear Lucas,

My name is Lucas too! I am 12 years old and I live in Lyon, France. I have one sister named Camille.

At school, I like Physical Education and History. After school, I play basketball with my team. On weekends, I like watching movies and spending time with my family.

Where do you live? What are your favourite subjects?

Write back soon!

Best wishes,
Lucas

tips: Start with a friendly greeting ('Dear [Name]', 'Hi [Name]').
Share basic personal information (age, city, school subjects).
Ask your recipient 2-3 simple questions to encourage a response.
End with a standard closing phrase ('Write back soon', 'Best wishes').

topic.title: My school
topic.description: Read a short text describing a school building, subjects, and daily routines.

readingPassage.title: My School: Oakridge Academy
readingPassage.text:
I go to Oakridge Academy. It is a big school with about 800 students. 

Our school day starts at 8:45 AM and finishes at 3:15 PM. We have six lessons every day. My favourite place in the school is the science laboratory because we do fun experiments. We also have a big football pitch and a library.

The teachers are friendly and helpful.

tips: State your school's name and general size.
Give start and finish times for the school day.
Mention school places (e.g., 'library', 'science lab', 'football pitch').
Use simple adjectives to describe teachers and facilities ('friendly', 'big', 'helpful').

topic.title: Trains and travel
topic.description: Read information and notices about train journeys to learn travel vocabulary, platform details, and ticket choices.

readingPassage.title: Train Travel Information
readingPassage.text:
Important Passenger Information:
- Trains to London depart from Platform 3 every 30 minutes.
- Single tickets are valid for one journey only. Return tickets allow travel back on the same route.
- Off-peak travel is cheaper and starts after 9:30 AM on weekdays.
- Passengers with seat reservations should board at least 5 minutes before departure.

tips: Distinguish between single tickets (one-way) and return tickets (two-way).
Look for key departure numbers like platform numbers and times.
Notice rules regarding off-peak savings and seat reservations.

topic.title: Travelling abroad
topic.description: Read a guide on airport procedures and travelling abroad to understand stages from check-in to flight takeoff.

readingPassage.title: Airport Step-by-Step Guide
readingPassage.text:
Step 1: Arrive at the airport 2 to 3 hours before your flight.
Step 2: Go to the check-in desk to drop off your luggage and get your boarding pass.
Step 3: Go through security and passport control.
Step 4: Wait in the departure lounge near your boarding gate.
Step 5: Board the plane when your gate number is called.
Step 6: Fasten your seatbelt as the plane prepares to take off.

tips: Use sequential order numbers or transition words (Step 1, Step 2, Next, Finally).
Learn key airport terms like 'boarding pass', 'passport control', and 'departure lounge'.
Pay attention to time guidelines before international flights.
